Linux2BE - Connecting your BE-300 to a Linux box.

Are you tired of having to boot Windoze for syncing your BE ? Well, then here's the right page for you.

1. You have to get a recent kernel release. I used 2.4.20-rc1, some versions of 2.4.19 were reported to not work. Earlier releases did not even include support for the CASIO device. You can get the kernel at your local ftp.kernel.org-mirror.

In order to compile the kernel, you have to extract it and afterwards go into menuconfig or xconfig and select the following:

First, you enter Network devices and select [*] Network device support and <M> PPP (point-to-point protocol) support
You will need the <M> support for async serial ports as well. [*] PPP filtering will be useful as well if you plan to go surfing with your PDA. You can also include <M> PPP Deflate compression and <M> PPP BSD-Compress compression.

Under USB support ---> <*> Support for USB has to be checked. You also have to include either the UHCI Alternate Driver (JE) support or the OHCI (Compaq, iMacs, OPTi, SiS, ALi, ...) support depending on your system.
At USB Serial Converter support you have to check <M> USB Serial Converter support (i.e as a module), as well as <M> USB Compaq iPAQ / HP Jornada / Casio EM500 Driver

As far as I know, this should be it. Save the configuration and run make dep clean bzImage modules modules_install

Now tell lilo to boot the new-made kernel in the kernel-source-subdir arch/i386/boot/bzImage and boot your new kernel.

2. Get SYNCE. SYNCE is a project that develops applications to connect Linux to your Windows CE PDA. They also have a little USB connection howto. Be sure to get at least version 0.4 of synce-serial. If you now, after inserting the usbserial and ipaq module into the kernel see a message in the kernel log (/var/log/messages) like

usbserial.c: Compaq iPAQ converter detected
usbserial.c: Compaq iPAQ converter now attached to ttyUSB0 (or usb/tts/0 for devfs)

Your USB connection works.
3.You start "synce-serial-start" as root after having done the synce serial setup like described on the synce website. If pppd starts well, everything should work fine. Try playing around with tools like "pls" or "pcp". Have fun !!


Common Errors:

ERROR: Usage of too old pppd.
SYMPTOMS: You get communication errors when trying to connect as well as "critical errors".
FIX: Simply get a newer pppd (either from your distributor or as source package). For me it was changing from ppp-2.4.1-51 to 2.4.1-170.


ERROR: No running dccm.
SYMPTOMS: After a few seconds of connection, you PDA says:
"Cannot start communications with the desktop computer. The computer is not available or busy and currently cannot accept connections."
FIX: The PDA discovers that nothing answers on the desktop computer at port 5679. This is the place where dccm should be running. Get it from the synce project and install it.
